_note: PEP-OWNED execution catalog for certification planning. It COMPOSES with configuration/containers_list.json (the authoritative platform source: that file owns which concrete containers, per architecture, are currently enabled/runnable). This file adds ONLY the two things the container list cannot express and that are genuinely certification policy: (1) supported_pg_majors — the PG majors PEP can currently execute for certification; (2) platforms — the bridge from a packaging OS token (as the detector/cert-plan emit it) to the container catalog's OS identities (catalog_os), where a container alias is '<catalog_os>-<arch>'. It never duplicates arch or enabled state, and it is NOT a fixed cell universe. Retire an OS by removing its platforms entry here (or disabling its containers in containers_list.json); add PG majors or platforms as data, no code change. Debian bullseye is intentionally ABSENT because it is EOL: historical bullseye build evidence therefore surfaces as an explicit unsupported coverage gap instead of silently disappearing. debian11 may remain enabled in containers_list.json for regression, but certification does not run on EOL bullseye.
